places.name: Aspen Grove Trailhead
places.access_note: Up the Alpine Loop past Sundance; the Stewart Falls trail starts from the south end of the Aspen Grove lot.

places.address: Cascade Springs Dr, off the Alpine Loop (SR-92), UT

ideas.title: Sunset walk up Rock Canyon
ideas.description: Walk a mile or two up the canyon as the rock walls catch the last light, then turn around and come down to the city lights. Free, close to town, and quiet enough to actually talk.
ideas.notes: Pin from OpenStreetMap (the trailhead). Address is descriptive; add the street if you want.

ideas.title: Bridal Veil Falls and a canyon stroll
ideas.description: An easy paved walk to the foot of a 600-foot double waterfall in Provo Canyon. Go in spring when it's roaring, or bundle up in winter when it freezes into ice. Bring a snack and sit by the river after.
ideas.notes: Pin from OpenStreetMap (the park). Check the paved trail is open; parts close for repairs some years.

ideas.title: Sunrise hike to the Y
ideas.description: Climb the switchbacks to the giant Y above BYU and watch the sun come up over the valley and Utah Lake. It's short but steep, so start in the dark with headlamps and reward yourselves with breakfast after.
ideas.safety_note: About a mile of steep switchbacks with no shade. Bring water and headlamps, and skip it when the trail is icy.
ideas.notes: Pin from OpenStreetMap (the trailhead).

ideas.title: Stewart Falls hike from Aspen Grove
ideas.description: A shady trail through aspens under Mount Timpanogos to a tall two-tier waterfall. About an hour each way at an easy pace, with plenty of spots to stop. In late September the whole mountain turns gold.
ideas.notes: Pin is Aspen Grove from OpenStreetMap, not the exact lot. Price assumes a canyon day-use fee split two ways: check the current fee.

ideas.title: Battle Creek Falls before dinner
ideas.description: A short, steady climb from a neighborhood park in Pleasant Grove to a waterfall you can walk right up to. Done in under two hours, so it pairs well with dinner in Pleasant Grove or Orem after.
ideas.notes: Pin and address are Kiwanis Park in Pleasant Grove (OpenStreetMap has it open dawn to dusk).

ideas.title: Tour Timpanogos Cave
ideas.description: Hike the steep paved trail up the side of American Fork Canyon, then follow a ranger through three connected caves full of helictites and crystal formations. It's cool inside even in July. Tickets sell out, so book a tour time first.
ideas.safety_note: The trail climbs about 1,000 feet in 1.5 miles with drop-offs. Tickets are required; book ahead.
ideas.notes: Price is a guess (tour ticket plus canyon fee): check current prices. Season dates vary by year.

ideas.title: Cascade Springs boardwalk
ideas.description: Drive the Alpine Loop to a hidden spot where springs bubble up and spill down a hillside in little terraced pools. Boardwalks and short paths wind through it. Go late in the day for golden light and a pretty drive home.
ideas.notes: Pin from OpenStreetMap (the springs). The Alpine Loop closes in winter. Price assumes a canyon fee split two ways.

ideas.title: Fall colors on the Alpine Loop
ideas.description: Take the winding mountain road from Provo Canyon to American Fork Canyon when the aspens and maples turn. Stop at Sundance for hot chocolate and wander the grounds, then pull over at every overlook you like on the way.
ideas.notes: Peak color is usually late September to early October. Price covers drinks and a canyon fee.

ideas.title: Mountain dinner at Sundance
ideas.description: Dress up a little and drive into Provo Canyon for dinner at Sundance Resort, tucked under Mount Timpanogos. Get there before sunset so you can walk the grounds first, then eat by the window.
ideas.notes: Check which restaurants are open and book a table. Price is a guess per person.

ideas.title: Sunset on Utah Lake
ideas.description: Walk out along the marina breakwater at Utah Lake State Park and watch the sun drop behind the western mountains. The sky reflects off the water for a long time after. Bring a blanket and something warm to drink.
ideas.notes: Price assumes the state park day-use fee split two ways: check it. Address is from OpenStreetMap (the campground).

ideas.title: Bike the Provo River Parkway
ideas.description: Ride the paved trail along the Provo River from Riverwoods toward the canyon, past cottonwoods and little bridges. Go as far as you like, then turn around and grab a treat in Riverwoods at the end.
ideas.notes: Bring your own bikes (or walk it). Pin from OpenStreetMap (the parkway near Riverwoods).

ideas.title: Riverside picnic at Vivian Park
ideas.description: Pack sandwiches and lemonade and find a shady spot by the Provo River in the canyon. Watch the water, skip rocks, and maybe catch the old Heber Creeper train rolling past.
ideas.notes: Check the train line still runs past (Heber Valley Railroad); drop that line if not.

ideas.title: Saturday morning at the farmers market
ideas.description: Wander the Provo Farmers Market at Pioneer Park with a pastry in hand. Taste samples, pick out fruit for the week, listen to whoever's playing, and grab something new to cook together that night.
ideas.notes: Hours from OpenStreetMap (Saturdays 9-2). Check the season dates for this year.

ideas.title: Ice skating at the Peaks
ideas.description: Skate where the 2002 Olympic hockey games were played. Hold hands, laugh when someone wobbles, and warm up with hot chocolate after. Public skating times change, so check before you go.
ideas.notes: Price is a guess (admission plus skate rental): check current prices and public skate times.

ideas.title: Wander the BYU Museum of Art
ideas.description: Free, quiet, and usually not crowded. Each of you picks a favorite piece in every gallery and explains why, then compare notes over a scoop of BYU Creamery ice cream just up the road.
ideas.notes: Closed Sundays. Pin from OpenStreetMap; hours not listed there, so add them.

ideas.title: Ice cream at the BYU Creamery
ideas.description: A Provo classic: huge scoops of ice cream made on campus, for not much money. Order a flavor you'd never pick for yourself and trade halfway through.
ideas.notes: OpenStreetMap's hours use month ranges the app can't read, so hours are unknown here. Closed Sundays. Address to confirm.

ideas.title: Rockwell ice cream and a downtown stroll
ideas.description: Get a cone of something adventurous at Rockwell on University Avenue, then walk Center Street looking in shop windows and at the old buildings. An easy end to any downtown dinner.
ideas.notes: Hours from OpenStreetMap: check they're current.

ideas.title: Dirty soda and a drive
ideas.description: Order two custom sodas you've never tried, then take a slow drive with the windows down and your favorite playlist. Utah's most Utah date, and it fits into any free half hour.
ideas.notes: Hours from OpenStreetMap. A chain: per the place policy this may be better as a stop than a featured idea.

ideas.title: Fry bread at Black Sheep Cafe
ideas.description: Native American and Southwestern food in downtown Provo: posole, Navajo tacos on fry bread, and green chile. Share a few plates so you both get to try everything.
ideas.notes: Address and pin from OpenStreetMap. Confirm it's open and add hours. Price is a guess.

ideas.title: Farm-to-table dinner at Communal
ideas.description: A dressed-up night out in downtown Provo, with seasonal dishes made from local ingredients. Order a few things to share and save room for dessert.
ideas.notes: Pin from OpenStreetMap. Confirm it's still open, the menu style, and reservations. Price is a guess.

ideas.title: Curry night at Bombay House
ideas.description: A long-time Provo favorite for Indian food. Order something milder and something spicier, plus a pile of garlic naan, and split everything down the middle.
ideas.notes: Pin from OpenStreetMap. Add the street address and hours. Price is a guess.

ideas.title: Comfort food at Station 22
ideas.description: Southern-style comfort food on Center Street, like fried chicken and mac and cheese. Casual, filling, and right in the middle of downtown, so you can walk it off after.
ideas.notes: Address and pin from OpenStreetMap. Add hours. Price is a guess.

ideas.title: Pizza at Brick Oven
ideas.description: Provo has been doing first dates at Brick Oven for decades. Get a pizza to share and the root beer, and ask each other the questions you never got around to asking.
ideas.notes: Address, pin and hours from OpenStreetMap. Check the root beer line is still true.

ideas.title: French toast breakfast at Kneaders
ideas.description: Start a Saturday slowly with the all-you-can-eat French toast and a hot drink. Linger over plans for the day, then walk the Riverwoods trail by the river right next door.
ideas.notes: Address and pin from OpenStreetMap. A chain (see the place policy). Check the French toast deal and hours.

ideas.title: A show at Velour
ideas.description: Catch a local band at Velour, the small downtown venue that launched a lot of Provo's indie acts. Look up who's playing, get there early for a good spot, and grab a late dessert after.
ideas.notes: Address and pin from OpenStreetMap. Ticket prices vary by show (this is a guess). Add the website for the calendar.

ideas.title: A show at the Covey Center
ideas.description: See a play, a concert, or a comedy night at Provo's downtown performing arts center. Check the calendar, pick something neither of you would usually choose, and talk it over at dinner after.
ideas.notes: Address and pin from OpenStreetMap. Ticket prices vary (this is a guess). Add the website.

ideas.title: Musical at Hale Center Theater
ideas.description: An intimate theater in Orem with Broadway-style musicals and plays, where every seat is close to the stage. Make a night of it with dinner nearby before the curtain.
ideas.notes: Address and pin from OpenStreetMap, which may be outdated: confirm this is the right Hale theater and that it's still running shows here. Price is a guess.

ideas.title: Bowling and arcade at Fat Cats
ideas.description: Bowl a couple of games with a silly bet on the line (loser picks the next date), then spend your tickets in the arcade. Loud, easy, and good for a group too.
ideas.notes: Address, pin and hours from OpenStreetMap. Price is a guess.

ideas.title: BYU football game
ideas.description: Wear blue, get there early to soak in the tailgate crowd, and cheer from the stands with the mountains behind the field. Bring a blanket for November games.
ideas.notes: Ticket prices vary a lot by game (this is a guess). Only on game days: consider a holiday-style window later.

ideas.title: Stroll Ashton Gardens
ideas.description: Wander 50 acres of themed gardens at Thanksgiving Point in Lehi, with waterfalls, a big lawn, and a famous spring tulip festival. Find a bench, people-watch, and pick the garden you'd plant at home.
ideas.notes: Pin from OpenStreetMap. Price is a guess: check admission. About 20 minutes north of Provo.
